content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑fat Muenster cheese is a semi‑hard cheese made from cow’s milk, traditionally produced in the Münster region of Germany. The lower fat content makes it lighter while preserving its characteristic mild, nutty aroma and slightly sweet taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Muenster cheese gets its name from the city of Münster, where it was first produced in the 17th century.
Traditional Muenster is aged 4–6 weeks; the reduced‑fat version is aged a bit shorter to keep a tender texture.
The cheese melts well, making it popular for grilled sandwiches and casseroles.
Fat reduction is achieved by partially skimming the milk and adding low‑fat curd.
Muenster is often served in slices with fruit, bread, or melted over hot dishes.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Muenster provides about 25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Approximately 500 mg of calcium per 100 g helps strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Reduced fat
items.content: With fat content around 10 %, it fits better into lower‑calorie diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Probiotic cultures
items.content: Fermentation leaves live bacteria that may support gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Residual lactose can cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein, the main milk protein.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The cheese is moderately salty; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite reduced fat, it still provides about 250 kcal per 100 g.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced‑fat Muenster works well in sandwiches, melted in casseroles, grated over salads, or served with fresh fruit. Slice thinly or shred as needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 2‑3 weeks. Discard if mold develops or the cheese develops an off‑odor.
